messages:
deploy-bot: Safety throttle engaged for rollout inference/v4.1.0 — canary p95 latency = 2.45s (threshold 1.2s). Auto-shift: fallback-model@15% active. Rollout paused, rollback window 15m. :rotating_light:
olivia: saw the spike on embeddings-route, marking @raj oncall. any obvious flakiness?
raj: oncall. pulling traces now. do we have error rate rise or just latency?
mike: traces -> https://redwood-infra/traces/abc123 — looks like KV cache misses and a GC pause on host-gpu-12 around the same time. logs:
```
# kernel stderr snippet
WARNING: tensor-alloc fallback triggered
KVCache miss ratio: 0.38
```

sara: related to the new memory layout patch from yesterday? that change landed to v4.1.0.
olivia: product is seeing higher tail latency for customer-facing rerank calls. CS pinged. we should decide manual abort vs let the auto-fallback continue.
raj: quick criteria proposal: if p95 > 1.5x baseline AND error% > 0.5% over 5m, escalate to manual rollback. otherwise let fallback run and monitor another 10m.
mike: current numbers (last 6m): p95 = 2.45s (baseline 0.9s), errors = 0.8%. matches rollback criteria.
sara: strongly +1 manual rollback. Dedicated customers might see degradation.
emily: canary is already at 15%. if we abort, prefer partial rollback to 4.0.8 pinned for canary and dedicated gateway while we triage. avoid full global revert unless necessary.
olivia: ok plan: manual rollback canary+dedicated gateway -> pin to v4.0.8; keep hosted canary at fallback-model for safety. mike, can you execute and coordinate comms?
mike: executing now:
```
/deploy rollback --to v4.0.8 --scope canary,dedicated --reason "p95 regression after mem-layout change"
```

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by mike. Target: v4.0.8. Scope: canary,dedicated. ETA: ~4m. Notifying release-notes and cs-team.
mike: rollout command returned success, starting traffic shift. watching metrics.
raj: monitoring infra — checking GPU host health and cache hit rates.
olivia: drafting customer note: "We briefly rolled back a canary release to address a latency regression affecting a subset of customers. We're investigating root cause; no data loss. Contact support for impact details." tagging #customer-communications after draft.
sara: ops checklist: open incident ticket, attach traces, list commits in v4.1.0 (mem-layout + kernel opt). I'll add to ticket.
emily: FYI, leaving automated rollback disabled for v4.1.0 for now until patch validated. we should record this in release notes: 'auto-rollback suppressed — manual intervention used.'
mike: metrics trending down: p95 back to 0.95s for canary, errors 0.12%. canary stable. dedicated pools draining to v4.0.8.
olivia: good. once dedicated is stable, we'll schedule a follow-up postmortem and re-open a canary with a revert-of-mem-layout or fix.
raj: will collect host-level logs for postmortem and link in ticket.
sara: notifying billing/enterprise-ops for any SLA tickets.
mike: closing thread to move to incident ticket #INC-2026-482. will post timeline in incident. :white_check_mark:
